reason: The picture links muscle-development signals to activating muscle genes in developing cells.
expectation: The signals should guide some cells toward making muscle proteins.

effect: The signals produced young muscle cells whose muscle genes are active, but they do not yet have the fibre bundles.
reaction: It is interesting that the cells keep the same chromosomes while using different genes.
reason: The young muscle cells need to make proteins, and amino acids are their building blocks.
expectation: The cells should use the amino acids to make muscle proteins.

alternatives.reason: That could start the other goal, but I will follow the muscle cells first.

effect: The muscle cells now contain growing bundles of muscle proteins, completing the first goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the protein building blocks become visible bundles.
reason: The picture links the supporting-cell signals to activating support-protein genes in another group of cells.
expectation: The signals should guide some cells toward becoming supporting cells.

effect: The signals produced young supporting cells with support-protein genes active, but they do not yet have a surrounding fibre network.
reaction: The parallel with the muscle cells makes the next step clearer.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and the supporting cells need to make fibres.
expectation: The cells should use the building blocks to make support proteins and surrounding fibres.

effect: The supporting cells made fibres around themselves, completing the second goal. The result also showed that cells can use the same DNA and building blocks for different jobs.
reaction: It was interesting that the supporting cells released proteins around themselves, while the muscle cells kept their protein bundles inside.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making both kinds of cells worthwhilely showed how the same DNA can support different jobs, with proteins ending up in different places.

leastWorthwhile.text: The supporting-cell sequence felt a little repetitive after the similar muscle-cell sequence, though the different result helped explain its purpose.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the supporting cells built a fibre network around themselves rather than keeping the proteins inside like the muscle cells.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary: the signal pictures named the cell types, and amino acids were identified as protein building blocks. I followed those clues rather than knowing exactly how the signals work.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter to see how these different cells work together, although the repeated signal-and-building-block pattern could get predictable.
